  1. Show HN: ExitPath – Open-source ways out of Slack, Notion and Microsoft 365

    • Open Source
    • Self-Hosting

    249 points · 93 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 16:04 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — ExitPath is a no-account, browser-local migration planner/catalog for leaving 19 proprietary tools, including Slack, Notion, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365. It lists 41 open-source alternatives and 60 migration paths, adjusts effort grades by team size and hosting choice, and offers checklists; it explicitly says most catalog entries are unreviewed AI drafts.

    Discussion — Readers found the consolidated catalog useful but stressed that migration pain is operational as well as technical: calendaring, identity/SSO, integrations, usability, and self-hosting burden. Zulip received positive firsthand reports; commenters disputed or refined particular recommendations and requested broader project-management coverage.

    Week of 2026-11-20

  2. Show HN: Sutra-OS – A self-hosted ontology platform

    • Databases
    • Self-Hosting

    72 points · 37 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 23:25 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Sutra-OS is an open-source, self-hosted ontology platform for representing data as typed, linked, actionable units governed by rules with source traceability. The repository calls it beta and says portions of the model language, APIs, UI, and documentation remain unfinished.

    Discussion — People asked whether it replaces database and knowledge-management tools and questioned ontology as a model for human decisions. The author described it as an abstraction layer that can query and write back to multiple systems; commenters raised governance and usability concerns.

    Week of 2026-11-20

  3. Ask HN: What is the state of self-hosting email in 2026?

    • Email
    • Self-Hosting

    48 points · 36 comments · 13 Nov 2026, 19:06 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The Ask HN post asked about the practical state of self-hosting email in 2026.

    Discussion — Respondents described self-hosting as possible but operationally demanding because of deliverability, reputation, monitoring, abuse handling, and redundancy. Many recommended relaying outbound mail through a specialist, ISP, SES, Zoho, or another managed provider.
